The glacier's constant movement is particularly impressive. Enormous blocks of ice gradually break away from its edge and crash into the lake, sending up waves and offering a reminder of the power of nature. This extraordinary sight lets visitors witness how a glacial landscape changes and evolves.

A visit to Perito Moreno offers several ways to experience the glacier. Walkways and viewing platforms provide panoramic views of the ice field, while a boat trip brings visitors closer to its majestic front. For those seeking a more active experience, guided walking excursions on the glacier are available with experienced specialists.

### Petén and the island city of Flores

Petén is Guatemala's largest department, covering an area of 35,854 square kilometres. Its municipality includes the island city of Flores, which also serves as a departure point for visits to a range of tourist attractions.

Petén has exceptional historical value thanks to its archaeological heritage, wildlife and biosphere reserve. Its numerous archaeological sites make the region one of the important centres of the Maya world.

## Holidays in Petén

### Petén — the cradle of the Maya!

Petén is the setting for many legends of one of the world's most remarkable cultures. Its fascinating archaeological sites are surrounded by jungle. Among them is Tikal, which UNESCO designated a World Heritage Site in 1979. Here you can explore Yaxhá, Seibal, Aguateca, San Bartolo and El Mirador, home to the largest Maya pyramid. Another notable site is Uaxactún, where an astronomical observatory once stood. Together, these places illustrate the development of Maya civilisation. The legendary quetzal also lives here, a bird that existed long before the Aztec and Maya peoples and that they regarded as a guardian of the air and a symbol of goodness and light.

Petermann Island lies on the western side of Penola Strait, between Hovgaard Island and the Argentine Islands. This small island combines rocky ground and snow, with the mountains of the Antarctic Peninsula rising across the water.

The island is named after the German geographer and cartographer August Petermann. It is visited on sea expeditions south of the Lemaire Channel. Itineraries in this area include opportunities to watch penguins and seabirds; conditions for approaching and landing are determined by ice and weather.
